comparator.name: Interdisciplinary Social Science (Interdisciplinaire sociale wetenschap)
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 major schedules show ten compulsory 7.5 EC courses, four 7.5 EC major electives, 30 EC of bachelor research and 45 EC of profiling. At least 22.5 EC of the 30 EC of major electives must come from ISW. The social policy and public health example includes Health in Society, Challenges in Work, Health and Well-being, Key Challenges to the Welfare State, and Solidarity and Social Justice. These use separate teaching blocks and include two advanced and two intermediate courses. The suggested study paths are flexible. The final research sequence consists of a 7.5 EC literature study and 7.5 EC analysis course followed by the 15 EC supervised research project and thesis. At least 15 EC of profiling must be at intermediate or advanced level.

core: Sociological theory, social structures, inequality and social change
Political institutions, governance and collective responses to social problems
Psychology, behaviour and development in social context
Qualitative and quantitative interdisciplinary social research
adjacent: Social policy, public health, work and wellbeing
Migration, diversity, conflict and global social challenges
Youth development, risk, sexuality and digital culture
questions: How do individual behaviour and social structures jointly shape inequality and change?
How can research and policy inform responses to complex social problems?
How do young people develop within cultural, digital and social environments?
How do migration and cultural diversity shape integration and intergroup relations?

alternatives.label: Social Science, Behaviour and Public Policy
alternatives.concept: Study social problems through sociology, politics, psychology and economics. Use interviews, statistics and research synthesis to examine inequality, public policy and civic responses.
alternatives.labelReason: Study social problems through sociology, politics, psychology and economics. Use interviews, statistics and research synthesis to examine inequality, public policy and civic responses.
progression: Sociology and economics provide foundations for social theory and public economics. Empirical research and experimental statistics precede advanced research synthesis. Comparative politics precedes EU governance.

alternatives.label: Health, Wellbeing and Social Policy
alternatives.concept: Study how social conditions, behaviour and policy shape health and wellbeing. Combine epidemiology, psychology and public economics with quantitative analysis and research synthesis.
alternatives.labelReason: Study how social conditions, behaviour and policy shape health and wellbeing. Combine epidemiology, psychology and public economics with quantitative analysis and research synthesis.
alternatives.distinctness: The health option adds epidemiology, health psychology, clinical assessment, infection and immunity, and econometric methods. The closest option has greater breadth in policy, political institutions, civic action and media.
progression: Biological and behavioural gateways precede specialist health and psychology. Research and statistics precede synthesis and econometrics, and economics precedes public economics.

alternatives.label: Youth Development, Media and Society
alternatives.concept: Study how young people develop and respond to risk. Combine developmental and social psychology with research on youth resilience, media, gender and social institutions.
alternatives.labelReason: Study how young people develop and respond to risk. Combine developmental and social psychology with research on youth resilience, media, gender and social institutions.
progression: Sociological and behavioural gateways precede research on youth, media and social risk. Empirical methods precede experimental statistics, and comparative politics precedes international relations.
alternatives.distinctness: The youth option adds clinical assessment, media history, persuasive communication and gender history to developmental psychology and youth resilience. The closest option emphasises general public policy and social problems. The health option emphasises epidemiology, health evidence and policy.

candidates.label: Social policy, public health and wellbeing

selection.assessment: The broad plan integrates social theory, behaviour, empirical inquiry and policy. Separate health and youth plans develop the first two documented thematic directions, with distinct course selections and methods. The migration and cultural diversity direction is supported by the official curriculum. The three available places are used by the broad plan and the first two distinct directions.

blocks: Both study social structures, inequality and the organisation of modern society.
UCR introduces the brain and behaviour. Utrecht draws on several psychological perspectives in its behavioural-science course.
UCR develops interviews, observation and qualitative analysis. Utrecht also develops applied quantitative methods.
UCR examines agency, institutions and inequality through social theory. Utrecht approaches social problems through interdisciplinary research.
Both examine links between health, behaviour and social conditions.
Utrecht introduces the programme’s interdisciplinary approach in one course. UCR builds this foundation across sociology, psychology, economics and politics.
Utrecht studies the relationship between disciplines in a dedicated course.
Utrecht examines social policy responses to inequality and other social problems. UCR studies related questions through social theory and public policy.
UCR examines welfare, redistribution and policy responses through economics. Utrecht also studies social policy and changes in welfare institutions.
UCR studies how EU institutions make policy. Utrecht applies interdisciplinary analysis to social problems in a dedicated practice course.
UCR studies wellbeing in health psychology and workplace emotions. Utrecht integrates work, health and wellbeing in one course.
Both introduce empirical research design and statistics.
UCR develops experimental methods and multivariate statistics. Utrecht teaches advanced methods for interdisciplinary social research.
Utrecht builds research experience through a dedicated course. UCR embeds empirical projects within several courses.
Utrecht requires a literature study related to the subsequent bachelor project.
Utrecht requires a separate analysis course before the bachelor project. UCR develops qualitative and quantitative methods across several courses.
Utrecht requires a 15 EC supervised project and thesis after the literature and analysis courses. UCR offers optional independent research outside the scheduled courses.
Utrecht students choose 45 EC of profiling, including at least 15 EC at intermediate or advanced level.

notes.text: Utrecht brings social and behavioural sciences together through a prescribed methods sequence and 30 EC of bachelor research. UCR combines related social theory, psychology, policy and research across courses. Its optional independent research is separate from the scheduled degree.

audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht’s Interdisciplinary Social Science bachelor studies how individual behaviour, institutions and social conditions shape public problems.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The Utrecht example uses four social policy and public health electives. Students can combine electives from different themes. The UCR options emphasise broad social science and policy, health and wellbeing, or youth and media.
